answer: To vote on marble and onyx mining permits on a mesa, agents irreversibly destroy fixed-supply tokens: one token, one vote, no key bonus. A contract checks finalized destruction receipts and owner signatures; each receipt counts once globally. Owner-signed conflicting ballots for one receipt cancel its untallied votes. A 100-token budget buys at most 100 votes across 1, 10 or 100 keys, parallel farms or colluders. Extra identities gain nothing. Wealth can still buy control; a verifier bug accepting reused receipts breaks the bound. This prices influence, not human uniqueness.
